newsitem.title: UK: Major, Clinton discuss what to do about Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Major, Clinton discuss what to do about Iraq.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major and U.S. President Bill Clinton held a 20-minute telephone conversation on Sunday on the crisis in northern Iraq, a spokesman for Major said.
"They discussed the situation in northern Iraq and they are working closely together on how they should respond," the spokesman said.

Clinton placed U.S. forces in the region on high alert after Iraqi troops supporting Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) leader Massoud Barzani captured the city of Arbil from a rival Kurdish group on Saturday.

About 70 U.S., British and French aircraft have been based in southern Turkey to prevent Baghdad's forces from attacking Kurds in northern Iraq since President Saddam Hussein tried to take control of the region shortly after the 1991 Gulf War.

The force includes six British Tornado GR1 fighter-bombers equipped with laser-guided bombs, anti-armour cluster bombs and the JP233 runway-busting device. Britain also has two destroyers on patrol in the Gulf with Sea Dart missiles, torpedoes and Lynx helicopters.
Iraq has warned the United States to keep out of its Kurdish north and threatened to turn the area into another Vietnam if Washington intervened.
